about.summaryTitle: About BMI: Formula, Health Classification & FAQ
about.formulaDesc: Body Mass Index (BMI) is an international screening metric developed by statistician Adolphe Quetelet. It estimates weight relative to height using the formula BMI = weight (kg) / [height (m)]².
about.boundary: Medical Note: BMI is an informational screening ratio and does not constitute clinical medical diagnosis, body fat percentage measurement, or cardiovascular risk assessment. Consult a licensed healthcare provider for individualized health advice.
about.descUnderweight: May indicate malnutrition, nutritional deficiency, or underlying physiological concerns.
about.descNormal: Associated with lower statistical risk of chronic cardiovascular and metabolic diseases.
about.descOverweight: Increased likelihood of elevated blood pressure and metabolic strain.
about.descObese: Significant clinical correlation with type 2 diabetes, joint stress, and cardiovascular issues.
about.faq1A: A: BMI divides weight in kilograms by height in meters squared (kg/m²), or in imperial units, pounds multiplied by 703 divided by inches squared.
about.faq2Q: Q: Why doesn't BMI reflect body fat percentage?
about.faq2A: A: BMI cannot distinguish between lean muscle mass and fat tissue. An athlete with high skeletal muscle density may have a high BMI without excess adiposity.
about.faq3Q: Q: What is a healthy waist-to-height ratio alternative?
about.faq3A: A: Many clinicians supplement BMI with waist circumference or waist-to-height ratio (keeping waist under half your height) to assess visceral abdominal fat.
about.faq4Q: Q: Is my entered height and weight saved anywhere?
about.faq4A: A: Never. Calculations occur 100% locally on your device within your browser. No private biometric data is logged or sent to external servers.
